title: Environmental vulnerabilities (power, HVAC, fire, water)
goal_html: Groups act as a facilities/security triage team reviewing a day's worth of sensor alerts for a fictional data center, decide which alerts require immediate escalation, and propose a control for each category of environmental risk. Ties to LO 2.2.A (analyze environmental vulnerabilities) and the course skill Analyze Risk.
steps_html:
1. (5 min) Each group reads readings 1-3 (server-room-a) and decides individually which readings should escalate to on-call staff immediately.
  2. (5 min) Group discusses: readings 2 and 3 are both elevated in the same room, what does that combination suggest that either reading alone would not? Reach consensus and fill in "likely cause" and "control" for rows 1-3.
  3. (5 min) Repeat for readings 4-5 (server-room-b) and 6-7 (server-room-c), including deciding whether row 6-7 needs any escalation at all.
  4. (5 min) Each group opens the simulation and checks their triage decisions against the sim's scoring for the analogous scenarios; groups revise any incorrect calls.
  5. (5 min) Report-out: each group states one row where they initially disagreed internally and how they resolved it.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one member is the "on-call engineer" (decides whether to escalate and to whom), one is the "budget owner" (must justify the cost of any proposed control against the risk it reduces), and remaining members are "auditors" (challenge whether the proposed control actually addresses the stated cause). For row 1 (total power outage), the group must specifically debate UPS runtime versus generator start time and what the acceptable outage window is before escalation.
exit_html: Each student writes one sentence: "Reading X should [escalate / not escalate] because [reasoning tied to threshold or combined-signal rule], and [control] would reduce recurrence by [mechanism]."
